# Wardian Docs

Wardian is where local agent work becomes visible, durable, and malleable. Run
the CLI agents you already use in real project folders, inspect their sessions
and results, then save useful work as reusable prompts, skills, agent setups,
automations, or project context.

This file is an agent-readable index for the public Wardian documentation. Use the linked pages as the canonical docs source.

## Getting Started

- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/getting-started - Install Wardian, complete first-run setup, verify a provider, spawn the first agent, and inspect the first Inbox result.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/key-concepts - Learn the app layout, agent setup, reusable work, automation runs, and tailorability slope.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/ui-overview - Learn the title bar, navigation rail, agent roster, workspace areas, and common app surfaces.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/workbench - Open surfaces as tabs, split and merge panes, move and reopen tabs, zoom, restore, reset, and understand terminal presentation ownership.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/first-run-troubleshooting - Recover from launch, provider detection, terminal startup, Inbox, and CLI setup problems.

## Core Workspace

- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/agents-overview - Monitor agents with adaptive Auto, multi-card Grid, or focused Single layouts and switch cards between Terminal and Chat.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/grid - Map the former Grid page to the current Agents Grid mode.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/dashboard - Watch the whole fleet over a trailing window, read fleet-scaled bars and live state, and spot an agent behaving oddly.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/analytics - Look up how much agents, models, or providers did over a chosen period from a rows-by-time matrix.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/garden - Read the map of agents, automations, and skills where distance reflects shared workspaces, teams, worktrees, and deployments.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/watchlists - Group, select, sort, and monitor agents in the roster.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/inbox - Review completed work, important updates, approval requests, and action-needed items.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/source-control - Stage, diff, commit, sync, and manage agent worktrees.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/explorer - Browse an agent workspace or Wardian home from the app.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/browser - Run a real page inside the Workbench, drive it yourself or through `wardian browser`, and understand session lifetime and the one-driver rule.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/remote-control - Pair and use the Wardian remote PWA over HTTPS.

## Reuse and Agent Direction

- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/library - Manage reusable prompts, skills, and library item assignment.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/agent-memory - Save evidence-backed agent memory, inspect recall, and configure optional automation consolidation.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/command-panel - Send one-off broadcasts or starred prompts to selected agents.
- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/class-management - Define reusable agent setups used by spawn and clone flows.

## Automations

- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/automations - Build and run visual automations from the Wardian app.
- https://docs.wardian.org/automations/ - Start with the automation mental model, launch behavior, runtime state, and engine loop.
- https://docs.wardian.org/automations/building-automations - Use the automation canvas, block library, node settings, and variable assistant.
- https://docs.wardian.org/automations/node-reference - Reference automation node types and user-visible behavior.
- https://docs.wardian.org/automations/triggers - Understand manual runs, scheduled triggers, and live listeners.
- https://docs.wardian.org/automations/agent-assignment - Map automation roles to direct agents, fresh clones, or reusable assignment modes.
- https://docs.wardian.org/automations/troubleshooting - Diagnose common automation authoring and runtime failures.

## CLI and Agent Communication

- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/agent-messaging-tools - Use structured peer messaging, follow-up tasks, receiving, and correlated replies through managed Codex tools.

- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/cli - Use the Wardian CLI for agent inspection, live control, inter-agent messages, worktree assignment, and automation commands.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/ipc-events - Understand frontend/backend event contracts and runtime telemetry surfaces.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/tauri-command-reference - Reference Tauri command boundaries used by the UI and native runtime.

## Providers and Runtime

- https://docs.wardian.org/guide/provider-readiness - Verify provider CLIs, authentication, shell PATH, and runtime prerequisites.
- https://docs.wardian.org/providers - Compare supported providers and user-facing runtime expectations.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/provider-runtimes - Implement or debug provider-specific spawn, resume, and transcript behavior.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/pty-lifecycle - Understand PTY ownership, resize, output buffering, and terminal lifecycle rules.

## Developer Internals

- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/architecture - Read the high-level architecture for frontend, backend, state, and runtime boundaries.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/setup - Set up a development checkout and local verification environment.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/state-management - Understand persisted state, runtime state, and frontend state ownership.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/agent-memory - Understand the SQLite authority, startup injection, automation commit boundary, and provider-neutral recall architecture.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/automation-engine - Debug or extend deterministic automation execution.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/native-e2e - Pick the native E2E layer for PTY, invoke, provider, and filesystem behavior.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/release-updates - Configure, validate, and recover signed desktop release updates, including macOS notarization.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/package-manager-distribution - Publish and validate winget, Homebrew Cask, and Linux package-manager metadata from stable release artifacts.
- https://docs.wardian.org/developer/docs-maintenance - Maintain public docs, screenshots, and this agent-readable index.

## Project Context

- https://docs.wardian.org/features - Review the public feature overview.
- https://docs.wardian.org/os-support - Check platform support and OS-specific notes.
- https://github.com/wardian-app/Wardian - Inspect source, issues, pull requests, and repository-internal specs.
